newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SOCDET says Philippine well flows 6,578 bpd.
newsitem.headline: SOCDET says Philippine well flows 6,578 bpd.

text.p: Sydney Oil Co Drilling and Exploration Trust (SOCDET) said on Friday an extended well test in the Calauit-1B offshore well in the Philippines flowed at a stable rate of 6,578 barrels of oil per day for two hours from the 1606 - 1688 metre interval before being shut-in due to surface equipment problems.
The oil's API measured 21.4 degrees and there was no evidence of water, hydrogen sulphide or carbon dioxide, it said.
SOCDET said it now intends to run a production logging tool and recommence production testing before possible acidising of the perforations.
Calauit-1B was drilled in 1991 and is located in permit GSEC 77, in the Northwest Palawan basin.
Testing is expected to provide further information about the well's productivity, reservoir size and oil-water contact, the company said.
SOCDET is funding 67 percent of the testing and as a result will increase its stake in GSEC 77 to 43.4270 percent after the testing from 20 percent.

Other partners are Dragon Oil Plc 9.2058 percent, Sinophil Corp, 1.25 percent, Palawan Oil and Gas Exploration, 1.25 percent, Oriental 6.7273 percent, PNOC Exploration Corp, 19.9775 percent, Coplex Resources NL 8.1685 percent, Phoenix Co of the Philippines, 5.0 percent, Basic Petroleum and Minerals Inc 3.494 percent and Trans-Asia Oil and Mineral Development Corp, 1.5 percent.
